description: I'm building an interactive web application using NASA SPHEREx observations to compare astronomical images, visualize changes over time, and investigate moving or variable objects. The project will include image comparison, basic object analysis, and AI-assisted explanations to make astronomical observations easier to explore and understand.
summary:
Cosmic Find is an interactive astronomy exploration platform that makes NASA's SPHEREx infrared observations easier to discover, visualize, and analyze.

Astronomical datasets are often difficult for students, researchers, and the public to explore without specialized software. Cosmic Find addresses this challenge through a user-friendly web application where users can enter celestial coordinates, locate matching SPHEREx observations, view infrared imagery, and explore changes across observation dates.

The platform combines a visual sky map, observation timeline, animated time-lapse, and image comparison tools. Its Python-based analysis pipeline aligns astronomical images using World Coordinate System (WCS) information and highlights candidate changes between observations.

Built with React, FastAPI, Python, and NASA/IPAC astronomical data, Cosmic Find bridges the gap between complex scientific archives and accessible visual exploration.

Our goal is to make space data more approachable, encourage scientific curiosity, and provide a foundation for further investigation of interesting astronomical changes.
details:
Cosmic Find — Project Details

The Problem

NASA's astronomical missions generate valuable scientific observations, but accessing and interpreting these datasets often requires specialized knowledge and software. Students, educators, citizen scientists, and independent researchers may struggle to locate relevant images, understand their spatial coverage, and compare observations taken at different times.

Our Solution

Cosmic Find is a web-based astronomy exploration and analysis platform built around publicly available NASA SPHEREx infrared observations.

Instead of manually searching through astronomical archives and processing FITS files, users can explore observation coverage through an interactive interface, search using celestial coordinates, inspect infrared images, and compare observations over time.

How It Works

  1. Sky Exploration: Users enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates to search for observations covering a specific region.
  2. NASA Archive Integration: The Python backend retrieves and indexes SPHEREx observation metadata from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive.
  3. Spatial Matching: World Coordinate System (WCS) information is used to determine whether the requested coordinates fall within an observation's image footprint.
  4. Infrared Visualization: Astronomical FITS image data are processed into browser-friendly visualizations.
  5. Observation Timeline: Matching observations can be viewed chronologically and explored through time-lapse playback.
  6. Temporal Analysis: Images are spatially aligned and compared to highlight candidate changes between observations.
  7. Scientific Interpretation: The platform presents exploratory comparison results while distinguishing potential changes from confirmed astronomical discoveries.

Working Prototype

The prototype includes a demonstration region at RA 321.194433° and Dec +24.181670°, with four matching observations from May 14, 2026.

For this region, the analysis pipeline produces four aligned frames and an exploratory difference map. In one test, the pipeline evaluated 65,516 common pixels and flagged 2,949 candidate residual pixels above a 5σ threshold.

These results represent preliminary image differences, not verified transient objects or astronomical discoveries.

Technologies Used

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, HTML, CSS

Backend: Python, FastAPI

Scientific processing: FITS image handling, astronomical WCS coordinate transformations, image alignment, and numerical image comparison

Data: Public NASA SPHEREx observations accessed through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive

Development and version control: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub

Innovation

Cosmic Find combines astronomical archive search, sky visualization, observation playback, and exploratory temporal comparison in one accessible workflow.

Its distinguishing feature is the integration of scientific coordinate-aware image processing with an interface intended to make complex infrared observations easier to explore.

Intended Impact

Cosmic Find aims to support astronomy education, citizen science, and early-stage research exploration by lowering the technical barriers to working with real space observations.

Future improvements could include more robust transient candidate filtering, uncertainty estimation, additional astronomical datasets, and publicly hosted processing services.

Limitations

The current analysis is exploratory. Differences can arise from noise, calibration variations, image alignment, wavelength differences, or instrumental effects. Candidate detections require additional validation before any scientific interpretation.
